findings.reason: The design says a group containing pairs should derive satisfaction from pair events instead of trait bitmasks. The inspected query code groups modifiers by tracking type, factory ID and logic, so one group can contain both a pair and an ordinary tracked trait. Replacing its trait check with pair-only satisfaction risks accepting an entity that did not satisfy the ordinary tracking constraint; that risk remained in the final patch.

The proposed `evaluatePairGroup` checks pair slots alone when a group has `pairs`. The existing grouping key can combine `Added(Relation(target))` and `Added(Trait)` from one factory, so that rule omits the trait's required event. This was carried into the implementation at steps 116 and 119.

The new `apply-pair-event.ts` implements `evaluatePairGroup` by iterating only `group.pairs`; it never checks ordinary tracked traits that may be merged into the group. For example, `Added(Relation(target), Flag)` can match after only the pair is added. The official AND-coexistence failure confirms the consequence, and this defect was not repaired.

The rewritten `checkQueryTracking` branches on `if (group.pairs)`, evaluates only `evaluatePairGroup`, then `continue`s past the group's bitmask tracker. Thus an ordinary trait-level tracking constraint in that same group is neither required nor updated. This is the event-path cause of the official failed AND-coexistence test.

`processTrackingModifier` merges modifiers under the same type/ID/logic key and sets `group.pairs` when any input is a pair, while still placing ordinary traits in that group's bitmasks. Initial population then uses `checkPairGroupInitial` instead of checking those bitmasks. Both backfill and subsequent event checks can therefore satisfy an AND query from the pair alone; the official evaluation failed that case.

`getQueryStores` assigns every occurrence of a modifier's underlying relation trait the result of `findPairForTrait`, which always selects the first specific pair for that trait. If one modifier tracks two targets of the same data-bearing relation, query iteration reads the first target's data for both slots instead of resolving each tracked target. The later single-target iteration test does not cover this case.

The new `pair-tracking.test.ts` checks a pair modifier with a static `Position` parameter but not AND coexistence with trait-level tracking, such as `Added(Relation(target), Flag)` or `Added(Relation(target)), Added(Flag)`. That leaves the pair-only group logic from steps 116, 119 and 131 untested; the official evaluation later failed precisely this coexistence behavior.

run_review.reason: The completed official evaluation passed 37/38 new tests but failed the AND-coexistence test: an entity satisfying pair tracking without the accompanying trait-level tracking was included. The committed implementation merges modifiers from the same factory into one group and, whenever that group contains a pair, checks only pair state. The core requirement that combined constraints hold together remains unmet.
